newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds firm, new issues trade higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds firm, new issues trade higher.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds were firm in a quiet session on Friday with bonds of CSX Corp's $2.5 billion deal bid higher throughout the day, traders said.

High-yielding issues were equally quiet, but prices gravitated higher as mutual funds recorded an influx of $760 million new cash in the week ended April 30. The number for the latest week marked a record for inflows to junk bond funds since AMG Data Services first compiled the data in 1992, the company said.
The cash flow number does not include distributions.

New issuance on Friday featured $325 million 9-3/8 percent senior notes from oil and gas well servicing contractor Pride Petroleum Services Inc, priced at par to yield 262.5 basis points over Treasuries. The issue rallied two points when freed, traders said.
"Everything is trading very strongly but it's also very quiet," one trader at a New York investment bank said.

Other high-yield new issues capitalizing on the more favorable environment included Allied Waste Industries Inc's 10-year, five-year zero coupon issue. The bonds, priced at 57.436 on Thursday were seen offered as high as 60 on Friday.

Analysts said the reemergence of zero coupon bond issues is a sure sign of renewed vigor in high-yields, while also noting the recovery has long to go before the structure regains popularity in telecommunication sector.
Telecom sector deals were the first issues to be postponed or cancelled when the market turned sour in March.

Next week's calendar features $900 million senior unsecured notes from Comcast Cellular Holdings, a newly formed holding company and unit of Comcast Corp. Proceeds from the notes will be used to redeem all zero coupon notes and repay some outstanding bank debt of Comcast Cellular Corp.

Other junk issues to price include: $300 million seven-year senior notes from Cityscape Financial Corp, $230 million 10-year senior secured notes from GST Telecom Inc, $100 million 10-year senior secured notes from French Fragrances Inc, and $100 million 10-year senior secured notes from Western Star Holdings Ltd.

Back in investment grade debt, dealers reported only light activity, suggesting bonds from the week's new deals found solid distribution. The lack of trading made levels difficult to judge, but most traders quoted unchanged spreads at mid-afternoon.
Bonds from Thursday's CSX deal tightened from attractive original levels -- five- and 10-year notes both tigthened one basis point on the bid side.

In the Treasury market, prices rose after the release of lower than expected job creation for April and a decline in hourly wages tempered inflation fears. But a drop in the unemployment rate from 5.2 percent to 4.9 percent, clouded the picture, analysts said.
Prices moved solidly into positive territory following news the Clinton Administration and Congressional leaders reached an accord to balance the Federal budget by 2002.
The benchmark 30-year bond was quoted up 10/32 at 96-21/32 to yield 6.89 percent at 1619 EDT/2019.

In equities, the Dow industrials rose 95 points. That brought gains for the week to 332 points, its largest weekly point gain ever. Technology stocks also bounded higher and the Nasdaq surged nearly 35 points, its largest one-day point gain in history.
